## Conference

### Talks and slides

::: {.gallery}

![V&V taxonomy for KG construction (Bosch) — speaker to add](assets/photos/conf/20260915_135745176.jpg){group="conference" fig-alt="Speaker with a microphone beside a screen showing a Bosch slide titled Verification & Validation Taxonomy for KG Construction" description="Slide: Verification & Validation Taxonomy for KG Construction — Conclusion & Outlook. The V&V taxonomy structures the field for industrial KG construction, to support neuro-symbolic / LLM-supported KG construction in industrial, safety-critical settings. Five dimensions: Evaluation Artefact, Reference Basis, Evaluation Perspective, Evaluation Executive, Temporal Execution. Reporting gaps observed in a manufacturing case study of 50 studies: syntax checks, dataset dependence, neural methods, evaluation perspective, reproducibility, structured reporting of V&V. Future work: extend to multimodal data (audio, image, video); validate generalizability to other safety-critical domains such as healthcare and autonomous driving. Slide © Bosch."}

![Q&A — a talk on Amsterdam Schiphol airport (title and speakers to add)](assets/photos/conf/20260916_103619482.jpg){group="conference" fig-alt="Two speakers on either side of a screen showing Questions? Let's discuss. over a photo of Schiphol airport"}

![Elody, an open-source data platform (Inuits)](assets/photos/conf/20260917_104605854.jpg){group="conference" fig-alt="Close-up of a browser showing github.com/inuits/elody-common and a tab named DAMS" description="Elody is a modular, open-source data platform developed by the Inuits community. It powers the Antwerp DAMS, which brings together the digital collections of the city's museums, libraries and heritage institutions, with linked data and IIIF. Code: github.com/inuits/elody-common"}

![How good are LLMs at Ontology Engineering? — closing slide](assets/photos/conf/20260917_134330889.jpg){group="conference" fig-alt="Slide asking whether an automatically generated ontology is really an ontology, listing competency questions and provenance" description="Slide (right edge cut off in the photo): Ultimately, is an ontology really an ontology if it has been automatically generated? (Gruber 92): an ontology is a formal specification of a shared conceptualization. AI improvements grow at a rapid pace; scores will likely improve in the months to come (with limitations like contamination). Key assets to ensure the outcomes from LLMs are useful: competency questions to drive ontology development; provenance — explain results in the benchmarks, not just provide numbers; explain why a term is added to an ontology, or why a CQ is proposed."}

:::
